# Formatting tells

## Markdown in the wrong place
Headings, bullets and bold pasted into email, wikitext, CMS fields or chat replies that should be prose. Check the target medium; default to paragraphs.

## Excessive bold
Bolding key phrases across every paragraph. Keep bold for warnings, UI labels or a term being defined. At most one or two per screen.

## Inline-header lists
"- **Scalability:** The system scales…" repeated for every bullet. Use prose or a table, or plain bullets without the bold lead-in.

## Title Case Headings
Use sentence case unless house style says otherwise.

## Over-structuring
Headings on a 200-word answer; lists with one item; nested bullets for linear ideas. Match structure to length.

## Em dashes
Heavy em dash use (several per paragraph) is a strong tell. Prefer commas, brackets, colons or full stops. Keep at most one per paragraph.

## Emoji
No emoji in headings, bullets or professional copy unless the brand voice requires it.

## Quotes and apostrophes
Mixed curly and straight quotes in one document suggests pasting. Normalise to house style.

## Citation and link residue
- URLs with `utm_source=chatgpt.com`, `utm_source=openai` or similar tracking params.
- Citation markers like `[1]`, `【4†source】`, `citeturn0search0`, `:contentReference[oaicite:0]`.
- Reference lists to sources that do not exist or do not support the claim. Verify every link.

## Broken markup
Stray `**`, unclosed code fences, markdown tables in places that don't render.
